the current framework for trauma sensitive schools is inadequate to address the needs of students in urban schools.
trauma sensitive schools are a growing trend in urban education and that the social justice implications of these schools have been inadequately addressed in existing frameworks.
trauma sensitive school initiatives are not social justice oriented and do not address social justice issues in the context of urban education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how trauma sensitive schools are conceptualized and implemented, and how they might be reimagined as a social justice intervention.
how the trauma sensitive schools movement can become a more robust social justice initiative.
the ways in which trauma sensitive school reform is being deployed in urban schools and how it is being used to justify and reproduce social inequalities in education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the trauma sensitive schools movement is a positive development, but it needs to move toward a more explicit focus on social justice in its approach to addressing the needs of students and families.
the current state of the art of trauma sensitive education is not sufficient for social justice education.

trauma sensitive approaches in schools are a social justice imperative, but the way that these initiatives have been implemented and conceptualized to date has not adequately addressed issues of equity and justice in schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trauma sensitive schools must be understood as a social justice imperative.
the authors are calling for a shift in how schools conceptualize trauma and the role of trauma in schools and the communities they serve.
trauma sensitive schools can only be fully effective when they address the root causes of the traumas that children experience.

trauma sensitive approaches to schooling can and must be grounded in a social justice framework.
the trauma sensitive school movement must be reoriented to center social justice in the design of trauma sensitive school initiatives and the development of school based interventions.
trauma sensitive schools can and should be a social justice project.
